subject: general
question: Who is known as the 'Napoleon of India'?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Samudragupta__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Samudragupta**:

 
 
• He ruled from **335 AD to 380 AD.**
 
• Samudragupta was the** greatest king of the Gupta dynasty.**
 
• The most detailed and authentic record of Samudragupta's reign is preserved in the **Prayaga Prasasti/Allahabad pillar inscription**, composed by his court poet **Harisena**.
 
• **Samudragupta’s military campaigns justify the description of him as the Napoleon of India by V.A. Smith. Hence, Option 2 is correct.**
 
• He assumed titles such as **Kaviraja Param Bhagavat Ashvamedha**- **parakrama Vikram Sarva-rajochchhetta **only Gupta ruler had the title of** Sarva-raj-ochchhetta.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skandagupta **repulsed the ferocious Hunas’ attacks twice.

 
 
• The heroic deed entitled him the title **Vikramaditya **(Bhitari Stone Inscription).
 
• He was the** last important ruler of the Gupta dynasty.**
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta II** was the son of Samudra Gupta and grandson of Chandragupta I.
 
 
• He assumed the title of Vikramaditya.
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta I:**
 
 
• He was the** first Gupta ruler **to assume the title of **Maharajadhiraja**.
